REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Singkawang.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Singkawang City.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
JDIH Kota Singkawang
6. Victim is a child and woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
7. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, the community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Special protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
10. Violence against women and children, hereinafter referred to as violence, is any act based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect, and preventing the ability of women and children to enjoy all their rights and freedoms.
11. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
13. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
14. Every person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
JDIH Kota Singkawang
16. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
17. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is a regional apparatus organization within the Singkawang City Government.
18. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against children and women from occurring.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
21. Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
23. Agency is a regional apparatus work unit whose duties and responsibilities are to coordinate the handling of affairs in the field of organizing the protection of children and women.
24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated, one-stop, and networked technical service established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions, and other institutions in efforts to empower women and protect women and children comprehensively from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations, and/or community organizations.
27. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of JDIH Kota Singkawang prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.
28. Task Force is a coordinative institution formed by the Regional Government that coordinates policies, programs, and activities for the protection of children and women in the region.
29. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the Regional Government, community, and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs, and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.

ELUCIDATION
OF
REGIONAL REGULATION OF THE CITY OF SINGKAWANG
NUMBER 4 OF 2017
CONCERNING
PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN
I. GENERAL
The implementation of protection for children and women is carried out based on the principles of humanity, integration and justice. So that every person must receive their right to protection against a sense of security and freedom from torture or treatment that degrades human dignity which is contrary to what is aspired to in the Preamble of the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia, namely the creation of a just and civilized humanity.

In Article 2 of Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, that the implementation of Child Protection is based on Pancasila and grounded in the 1945 Constitution of the Republic of Indonesia as well as the basic principles of the Convention on the Rights of the Child including:
a. non-discrimination;
b. the best interests of the child;
c. the right to life, survival, and development; and
d. respect for the views of the child.

In Article 3 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, that the elimination of domestic violence is implemented based on the principles of:
a. respect for human rights;
b. justice and gender equality;
c. non-discrimination; and
d. protection of victims.

In Article 3 of Law Number 23 of 2002 concerning Child Protection, that Child Protection aims to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and receive protection from JDIH Kota Singkawang violence and discrimination, for the realization of quality Indonesian children who are noble in character and prosperous.

In Article 4 of Law Number 23 of 2004 concerning the Elimination of Domestic Violence, that the elimination of domestic violence aims to:
a. prevent all forms of violence in the household;
b. protect victims of domestic violence;
c. take action against perpetrators of domestic violence; and
d. maintain the integrity of a harmonious and prosperous household.

To realize law enforcement and the fulfillment of the basic rights of children and women, the Government of the City of Singkawang is obligated to provide protection from acts of violence and discrimination as well as the fulfillment of civil rights and freedoms which are set forth in a policy at the regional level.

The establishment of a Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Children and Women is an elaboration of higher legislation that regulates the rights of children and women. In the Regional Regulation concerning the Protection of Children and Women, the norms formulated are efforts to address the problems faced in the implementation of protection of children and women in the City of Singkawang. The implementation of protection of children and women is carried out to realize the fulfillment of the rights of children and women in accordance with human dignity and dignity, and to receive protection from violence, discrimination, exploitation, and neglect for the realization of human resource development in the City of Singkawang that is faithful, intelligent, quality, noble in character and prosperous.

II. ARTICLE BY ARTICLE

Article 63
(1) Every company is prohibited from employing child labor under age or exploiting children.
(2) Companies must position female workers as work partners to grow the company.

Article 65
(1) For female workers who work beyond working hours, the company is obligated to provide overtime pay in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
(2) The company is obligated to protect occupational health and safety, as well as grant maternity leave rights to female workers.
JDIH Kota Singkawang (3) The company is prohibited from making policies that create discrimination against female workers.
(4) Companies that violate the provisions as referred to in paragraph (1), paragraph (2), and paragraph (3), may be subject to administrative sanctions in the form of:
a. verbal warning;
b. written warning; and
c. other administrative sanctions in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.

Article 23
(1) Every Person and/or Institution is obligated to protect children and women from violence, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and neglect.
(2) Protection by Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) by not implementing policies and actions that violate the rights of children and women.

Article 69
(1) Placement of child or female victims of acts of violence in temporary shelters as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out if based on identification results:
a. there is a threat to safety;
b. the child has no family/caregiver or guardian; and/or
c. the child cannot be reunited with family/caregiver/guardian and/or the community.
(2) Placement as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for a certain period of time while the child or victim receives recovery services and/or until the family/caregiver/guardian is assessed to have the readiness to care for and protect the child.
JDIH Kota Singkawang (3) Services provided to children and/or women while in temporary shelters include among others services for fulfilling basic needs and psychosocial assistance.
(4) The OPD responsible for social affairs is obligated to provide temporary shelters.
(5) The OPD responsible for social affairs may cooperate with the civil service police or the police in efforts to maintain the security of children or women whose safety is threatened while in temporary shelters.

CHAPTER VIII
ADOPTION OF CHILDREN
Article 18
(1) Adoption of children may only be carried out for the best interests of the child, and is carried out based on customary practices and in accordance with the Laws and Regulations.
(2) Adoption of children does not sever the blood relationship between the adopted child and his/her biological parents.
(3) Adoption of children must be recorded in the birth certificate without eliminating the child's original identity.
(4) Prospective adoptive parents must be of the same religion as the religion adhered to by the prospective adopted child.
(5) Adoption of children by foreign nationals may only be carried out as a last resort in accordance with the Laws and Regulations.
(6) In the event that the child's origins are not known, then the child's religion shall be adjusted to the religion of the majority of the local population.

1.6.rationale: In the original Indonesian text, harmful practices are explicitly addressed via child marriage prevention: Pasal 11 ayat (1) huruf d states parents must “mencegah terjadinya perkawinan pada usia anak” (prevent marriage at child age). That is a classic “harmful practice” (child/early marriage) and should yield Yes. None of the retrieved English candidates for 1.6 include Pasal 11, so retrieval missed the key evidence (RAG candidate issue). Additionally, the judge’s rationale claimed no explicit mention of early/child marriage; that would be incorrect if Pasal 11 had been retrieved, so the decision is also consistent with an evaluation failure contingent on missing retrieval.

(1) For the prevention of acts of violence against women, the Regional Government shall conduct empowerment and awareness-raising to families and communities by providing information, guidance and/or counseling.
e. providing education for victims of violence and vulnerable groups;
4.4.evaluator_rationale: Education/information provision is included as an explicit prevention approach: the policy requires awareness-raising by providing information/guidance/counseling to prevent violence against women, and lists providing education for victims of violence and vulnerable groups within prevention and protection efforts.

4.4.rationale: The original Indonesian text clearly includes prevention through education/awareness. Pasal 22 ayat (3) explicitly lists prevention efforts including “melakukan sosialisasi Peraturan Perundang-undangan…” and “memberikan pendidikan bagi korban kekerasan dan kelompok rentan,” plus “pendidikan pengasuhan keluarga/anak” and use of communication/information/education media. Pasal 62 ayat (1) also requires “pemberdayaan dan penyadaran… dengan memberikan informasi, bimbingan dan/atau penyuluhan.” The retrieved candidates contain these provisions and the judge’s reasoning matches them. Therefore the golden label ‘No’ appears inconsistent with the policy text and should likely be ‘Yes’.

5.3.evaluator_rationale: The candidate sentences refer to community participation, community leaders, and community institutions generally, but do not explicitly mention traditional/customary/cultural leaders, customary institutions, or customary dispute-resolution mechanisms.

(1) The mayor is obligated to conduct supervision of the implementation of child and women protection in the region.
(2) The community may conduct supervision of the implementation of child and women protection organized by the Regional Government through a mechanism of conveying aspirations to the mayor or the Regional House of Representatives.

Article 82
(1) In order to increase the effectiveness of supervision of the implementation of the fulfillment of children's rights, Regional Governments may establish a Regional Child Protection Commission or other similar institutions to support the supervision of the implementation of child protection in the region.
(2) The membership of the Regional Child Protection Commission consists of 1 (one) chairperson, 1 (one) vice chairperson, and 7 (seven) members.
(3) The membership of the Regional Child Protection Commission comes from elements of the Regional Government, religious leaders, community leaders, community organizations, the business sector, and community groups that care about child protection.

Article 9
(1) The obligations and responsibilities of the community as referred to in Article 7 are carried out in the form of community participation in the implementation of protection of children and women.

(2) Guidance as referred to in paragraph (1), is implemented in the form of:
a. guidelines and fulfillment standards;
b. technical guidance and training;
c. provision of facilities;
d. monitoring; and

JDIH Kota Singkawang (3) In the context of guidance as referred to in paragraph (2), the Regional Government may cooperate with the Central Government, other Regional Governments, Non-Governmental Organizations, the business sector and universities.

5.3.rationale: The original Indonesian text engages explicitly with “tokoh masyarakat” and “tokoh agama” (community and religious leaders) in stakeholder structures. For example, Pasal 82 ayat (3) states membership of the Komisi Perlindungan Anak Daerah comes from elements including “tokoh agama” and “tokoh masyarakat”; Pasal 89 ayat (2) similarly includes “tokoh agama, tokoh masyarakat” in the KLA task force. The retrieved English candidates include this (e.g., Article 82(3) mentioning religious leaders and community leaders). If the indicator is about engaging traditional/cultural community leadership (not strictly “customary/adat” institutions), this is satisfied and the judge was overly narrow by requiring explicit “adat/traditional/customary” wording. Thus the golden ‘Yes’ is supported by the text and evidence; the predicted ‘No’ seems wrong due to an overly strict interpretation, but since the judge’s stated criterion was “traditional/customary/cultural leaders,” the more fundamental issue is that the indicator/golden likely treats community leaders as qualifying engagement. Hence golden label is plausible and the discrepancy stems from evaluation strictness; however because the evidence was present and the judge still said No, this is best categorized as evaluation_failure.

6.5.evaluator_rationale: The cited disability-related measures concern children with disabilities (e.g., special needs fulfillment and inclusive/special education) and do not specify special protection measures targeted at women with disabilities or people with disabilities generally in the context of women’s protection.

Article 45
Special protection for child victims of riots, disaster victims, and children in armed conflict situations as referred to in Article 43 letters b through d shall be implemented through:
a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of food, clothing, shelter, education, health, learning, and recreation, security guarantees, and equal treatment; and
b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities and children experiencing psychosocial disorders.

Article 21
(1) Planning for the protection of children and women is implemented by providing data and information related to the protection of children and women in the region.
(2) Data and information as referred to in paragraph (1) concerns data on gender mainstreaming (PUG), data on child rights mainstreaming (PUHA), and evaluation of programs and data services.
(3) Data and information as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be provided by the OPD that administers the affairs of child and women protection.
(4) Data information as referred to in paragraph (3) is required for policy planning and program intervention coordinated by the Agency.

Article 33
(1) Children with disabilities are given opportunities and accessibility to obtain inclusive education and/or special education.
(2) Children who have excellence are given opportunities and accessibility to obtain special education.
(3) Children who receive special protection are given opportunities to obtain their right to education.

Article 36
(1) Regional Governments are obligated to develop child-friendly school models. (2) Child-friendly schools as referred to in paragraph (1) constitute a joint effort of school community members to:
a. create a safe and comfortable environment for children at school;
b. develop child participation in accordance with their age and maturity; and c. provide opportunities for children from poor families and/or persons with disabilities to receive equal and fair treatment in obtaining services and guidance at school.

Article 23
(1) Every Person and/or Institution is obligated to protect children and women from violence, exploitation, discrimination, mistreatment and neglect.
(2) Protection by Institutions as referred to in paragraph (1) by not implementing policies and actions that violate the rights of children and women.

Article 75
(1) Law enforcement services constitute actions by law enforcement officials in implementing Laws and Regulations to handle cases of violence against children and women, especially to impose sanctions on perpetrators and provide protection for witnesses and/or victims.
(2) Law enforcement services as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out by prioritizing the best interests of children and women victims of violence.
(3) Law enforcement services are aimed at providing protection for children and women victims of violence or children in conflict with the law with a gender-responsive approach so that victims and perpetrators obtain justice and legal certainty.
(4) For the purpose of implementing law enforcement as referred to in paragraph (1), the Regional Government in cooperation with relevant agencies and institutions shall allocate resources to encourage the achievement of effectiveness and efficiency of law enforcement services for children and women victims of violence and children in conflict with the law in accordance with applicable provisions.

6.5.rationale: The original Indonesian text covers disability not only for children but also for women. Pasal 2 ayat (2) huruf f states: “khusus bagi perempuan penyandang disabilitas, berhak untuk mendapatkan kemudahan dan perlakuan khusus dalam pelayanan publik” (women with disabilities have the right to facilities and special treatment in public services). This directly supports a Yes for a disability/intersectional indicator. The retrieved candidates shown to the judge only included child-disability provisions (e.g., Pasal 33, Pasal 45, Pasal 98(h)) and missed Pasal 2(2)(f). So retrieval failed. Additionally, the judge concluded No because measures were only for children; that conclusion would be incorrect relative to the full policy, but given the missing passage it is primarily a RAG candidate issue. Still, the judge also overlooked that even within retrieved text there is at least a general non-discrimination/protection duty (Pasal 23) and a prohibition on discriminating against children with disabilities (Pasal 98(h)), which may or may not satisfy the indicator depending on its scope. The key miss is Pasal 2(2)(f).

6.10.translated_snippet: Special protection for children who become refugees as referred to in Article 43 letter a shall be implemented in accordance with the provisions of Laws and Regulations.
6.10.evaluator_rationale: The policy includes special protection for children who become refugees, indicating that refugee status is explicitly covered by special protection measures (even though framed for children).

(1) Placement of child or female victims of acts of violence in temporary shelters as referred to in Article 66 paragraph (2) letter c shall be carried out if based on identification results:

(2) Placement as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out for a certain period of time while the child or victim receives recovery services and/or until the family/caregiver/guardian is assessed to have the readiness to care for and protect the child.

Article 45
Special protection for child victims of riots, disaster victims, and children in armed conflict situations as referred to in Article 43 letters b through d shall be implemented through:
a. fulfillment of basic needs consisting of food, clothing, shelter, education, health, learning, and recreation, security guarantees, and equal treatment; and
b. fulfillment of special needs for children with disabilities and children experiencing psychosocial disorders.

REGIONAL REGULATION ON THE PROTECTION OF CHILDREN AND WOMEN.
CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is the City of Singkawang.
2. Regional Government is the regional head as an element of the Regional Government administration who leads the implementation of governmental affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
3. Mayor is the Mayor of Singkawang City.
4. Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including those still in the womb.
5. Woman is an adult human being of female sex and a person who is legally recognized as a woman.
JDIH Kota Singkawang
6. Victim is a child and woman who experiences misery and/or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of violence.
7. Protection of Women is all activities aimed at providing a sense of security carried out by the Regional Government, the community, and/or other parties who know or hear that violence against women will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
8. Child protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
9. Special protection is a form of protection received by children in certain situations and conditions to obtain a guarantee of security against threats that endanger themselves and their lives in their growth and development.
10. Violence against women and children, hereinafter referred to as violence, is any act based on gender differences that results in misery or suffering physically, sexually, mentally, psychologically, including intimidation, forced eviction, threats of certain actions, coercion or deprivation of freedom, neglect, and preventing the ability of women and children to enjoy all their rights and freedoms.
11. Family is the smallest unit in society consisting of husband and wife, husband and wife and their children, or father and children, or mother and children, or blood relatives in a direct line upward or downward up to the third degree.
12. Parents are biological father and/or mother, or stepfather and/or stepmother, or adoptive father and/or adoptive mother.
13. Guardian is a person or body who in reality exercises parental authority as a parent over a child.
14. Every person is an individual or corporation, whether a legal entity or not a legal entity.
15. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to victims when seeing, hearing and/or knowing that violence against victims will occur, is occurring, or has occurred.
JDIH Kota Singkawang
16. Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of strengthening victims of violence to resolve the problems they face.
17. Regional Apparatus Organization, hereinafter abbreviated as OPD, is a regional apparatus organization within the Singkawang City Government.
18. Prevention is an activity carried out to prevent acts of violence against children and women from occurring.
19. Repatriation is an effort to return women and child victims of violence to their families, substitute families, or communities that can provide protection and fulfill their needs.
20. Rehabilitation is recovery from disturbances to physical, psychological, and social conditions so that they can carry out their roles again properly both in the family and in society.
21. Reintegration is an effort to reunite victims with their families, communities, institutions, or other social environments that can provide protection.
22. Institution is an agency/service/body/office within the scope of the Regional Government and/or non-governmental organizations that provide assistance.
23. Agency is a regional apparatus work unit whose duties and responsibilities are to coordinate the handling of affairs in the field of organizing the protection of children and women.
24. Integrated Service Center, hereinafter abbreviated as PPT, is a functional work unit that organizes integrated services for victims of violence.
25. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment, hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A, is an integrated, one-stop, and networked technical service established by the government, Regional Government, community, non-governmental organizations, donor institutions, and other institutions in efforts to empower women and protect women and children comprehensively from various types of discrimination and acts of violence, including human trafficking.
26. Community is individuals, families, groups, and social organizations, and/or community organizations.
27. Regional Action Plan, hereinafter abbreviated as RAD, is the foundation and guideline for relevant agencies, vertical agencies, and the community, in carrying out activities for the implementation of JDIH Kota Singkawang prevention and protection of children and women victims of violence.
28. Task Force is a coordinative institution formed by the Regional Government that coordinates policies, programs, and activities for the protection of children and women in the region.
29. Child-Friendly City, hereinafter abbreviated as KLA, is a city that has a child rights-based development system through the integration of commitments and resources of the Regional Government, community, and business world that are planned comprehensively and sustainably in policies, programs, and activities to ensure the fulfillment of children's rights.
